section_1.title: The 3D Mystery: Photo vs. Hologram
section_1.content: Introduction to the fundamental difference between traditional photography and holography. Explain that while photos record only brightness (intensity), holograms record the 'depth' and 'shape' of light waves.
section_1.example: An animated cat tries to pounce on a 2D photo of a mouse and fails to see depth, then encounters a 3D holographic mouse that it can walk around, seeing different angles as it moves.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Waves
section_2.content: Review of wave properties: Amplitude (brightness) and Phase (position in the wave cycle). Introduce Constructive and Destructive Interference as the 'building blocks' of holographic patterns.
section_2.example: Visualizing two pebbles dropped in a pond. Where the ripples meet and get taller is 'constructive' interference; where they cancel out is 'destructive'. Animation shows the peaks and troughs aligning.

section_3.title: The Recording Process: Making the Blueprint
section_3.content: Explain the setup of a laser beam split into two: The 'Object Beam' (hits the subject) and the 'Reference Beam' (stays pure). Their collision creates an 'Interference Pattern' on the film.
section_3.example: A laser beam hits a mirror. Half the light bounces off a 'Golden Dragon' figurine (Object Beam), while the other half hits the film directly (Reference Beam). The film looks like messy noise, not a dragon.

section_4.title: The Physics of Diffraction: Bending the Light
section_4.content: Introducing the concept of Diffraction. When light hits the microscopic 'interference pattern' (which acts like a complex grating), it bends. Introduce the simplified Grating Equation: d sin(θ) = mλ, using graphics to show how spacing (d) affects the angle (θ).
section_4.example: Animation of light passing through a picket fence. If the slats are close together, the light fan-out is wider. The 'messy noise' on the holographic plate is actually a trillion tiny 'fences' that bend light back into the shape of the original object.

section_5.title: Reconstruction: Bringing the Ghost to Life
section_5.content: Explain how shining the Reference Beam back through the processed hologram 'reconstructs' the wavefront of the original object through diffraction.
section_5.example: The 'Golden Dragon' is gone. We shine the laser through the 'noisy' plate. Because of the diffraction math (d sin θ), the light waves exit the plate exactly as they did when they bounced off the dragon. The cat from Section 1 sees the dragon's 'ghost' floating in space.

section_6.title: Real-World Diffraction: From Credit Cards to VR
section_6.content: Brief summary of applications. How microscopic diffraction gratings are used for security and modern head-up displays (HUDs).
section_6.example: Zooming into the shimmering dove on a credit card to show the microscopic lines, then transitioning to a pilot's helmet display showing holographic flight data overlaid on the real world.

I have drafted and set the initial animation steps for all six sections of the video ("The 3D Mystery: Photo vs. Hologram"). Although the final lecture lines are still pending from the ScriptWriter, I have provided codable animation descriptions based on the section titles and general subject matter to ensure the team can proceed with visual development.

- **Section 1:** Visualized the comparison between 2D photography and 3D holography using a camera, laser splitting, and a glowing 3D cube.
- **Section 2:** Illustrated wave physics (sine waves, phase peaks/troughs, and constructive interference).
- **Section 3:** Detailed the holographic recording process with a laser, beam splitter, object reflection (teapot), and interference pattern formation.
- **Section 4:** Showed diffraction principles using wave fronts passing through slits to create circular arcs and interference fringes.
- **Section 5:** Demonstrated holographic reconstruction where a laser shines through the pattern to form a virtual 3D image.
- **Section 6:** Applied concepts to real-world examples, including credit card security holograms and VR lens technology.

section_6.content: Brief summary of applications. How microscopic diffraction gratings are used for security and modern head-up displays (HUDs).
section_6.example: Zooming into the shimmering dove on a credit card to show the microscopic lines, then transitioning to a pilot's helmet display showing holographic flight data overlaid on the real world.

section_1.title: The 3D Mystery: Photo vs. Hologram
lecture_lines: Traditional photos record only the intensity of light waves.
They capture a flat, two-dimensional view of the world.
Holography captures both the intensity and the light's phase.
This records the three-dimensional shape of the light wavefront.
Moving your perspective reveals different angles of the object.
animations: A camera #FFFFFF takes a picture of a cube #B0C4DE, resulting in a flat 2D image appearing on a screen.
A laser beam #FF0000 splits; one part hits the cube while the other hits a plate #A9A9A9.
A glowing 3D cube #00FF00 emerges from the plate, rotating to show depth and perspective.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Waves
lecture_lines: Light waves have both amplitude and phase properties.
Interference happens when two light waves overlap.
Aligned peaks create brightness, while opposing peaks cancel out.
animations: A white sine wave #FFFFFF oscillates horizontally across the black background.
The peak of the wave flashes yellow #FFFF00 and the trough flashes magenta #FF00FF to show phase.
Two waves align their peaks, merging into a single wave with double the amplitude in cyan #00FFFF.

section_3.title: The Recording Process: Making the Blueprint
lecture_lines: A laser beam is split into two separate paths.
The object beam reflects off the subject being recorded.
The reference beam travels directly to the holographic film.
These beams collide, creating a complex interference pattern.
This microscopic pattern encodes the object's 3D information.
animations: A red laser #FF0000 hits a beam splitter, creating two separate beams.
One beam reflects off a teapot #B0C4DE onto a recording plate, carrying its shape data.
The second beam hits the plate directly, creating a complex interference fringe pattern #E6E6FA.

section_4.title: The Physics of Diffraction: Bending the Light
lecture_lines: Diffraction bends light as it passes through tiny openings.
Holographic patterns act as microscopic gratings for light waves.
This bending recreates the original path of the light.
animations: Parallel white wave fronts #FFFFFF approach a narrow vertical slit.
As the waves pass through, they transform into orange circular arcs #FFA500 spreading outward.
Multiple slits appear, creating a pattern of bright and dark spots #FF6347 on a distant screen.

section_5.title: Reconstruction: Bringing the Ghost to Life
lecture_lines: To see the image, we use the reference beam.
Illuminating the hologram causes the light to diffract.
The diffracted light waves perfectly mimic the original object.
We see a three-dimensional "ghost" of the recorded object.
The original wavefront is recreated, restoring depth and perspective.
animations: A red reconstruction laser #FF0000 shines through the developed holographic plate.
Blue light rays #87CEEB bend and diverge at specific angles from the plate's pattern.
The rays form a shimmering virtual image of the original object #F0FFF0 in mid-air.

section_6.title: Real-World Diffraction: From Credit Cards to VR
lecture_lines: Tiny diffraction gratings provide security on credit cards.
Head-up displays use these principles to project transparent data.
Holography brings 3D visuals to modern engineering and art.
animations: A silver credit card #C0C0C0 is shown with a bird-shaped hologram in the corner.
The card tilts, and the bird's color shifts smoothly from red #FF0000 to blue #0000FF.
A cross-section of a VR lens appears, showing light bending through tiny gratings #98FB98.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.5).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.0  # Shifted right to accommodate lecture
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.9
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Real-World Diffraction: From Credit Cards to VR"
        lines = [
            "Tiny diffraction gratings provide security on credit cards.",
            "Head-up displays use these principles to project transparent data.",
            "Holography brings 3D visuals to modern engineering and art."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a silver credit card
        card = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=2.0, width=3.2, 
                               fill_opacity=1, fill_color="#C0C0C0", stroke_color=WHITE)
        
        # Simple bird shape for hologram
        bird_body = Circle(radius=0.1, fill_opacity=1, color="#FF0000")
        wing_l = Arc(radius=0.3, start_angle=0.5*PI, angle=PI, color="#FF0000").rotate(0.5*PI)
        wing_r = Arc(radius=0.3, start_angle=0.5*PI, angle=PI, color="#FF0000").rotate(-0.5*PI)
        wing_l.shift(LEFT*0.1)
        wing_r.shift(RIGHT*0.1)
        bird = VGroup(bird_body, wing_l, wing_r).scale(0.5)
        
        # Position bird on the card
        bird.move_to(card.get_corner(UR) + DOWN*0.4 + LEFT*0.4)
        card_group = VGroup(card, bird)
        
        self.place_in_area(card_group, "B1", "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(card_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Tilt card and shift color
        self.play(
            Rotate(card_group, angle=20*DEGREES, axis=RIGHT),
            bird.animate.set_color("#0000FF"),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # VR Lens / HUD visualization
        # Lens cross section
        lens = Arc(radius=2, start_angle=-PI/4, angle=PI/2, stroke_width=8, color=BLUE_A)
        self.place_in_area(lens, "C4", "E6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Microscopic gratings on the lens (represented as fine dashes)
        grating_lines = VGroup(*[
            Line(UP*0.1, DOWN*0.1, stroke_width=1, color="#98FB98")
            for _ in range(10)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.05)
        grating_lines.move_to(lens.get_center())
        
        # Light ray projection
        light_ray = Line(self.grid["F4"], lens.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        bent_ray = Line(lens.get_center(), self.grid["B5"], color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Data overlay (HUD)
        hud_text = Text("ALT: 3000ft\nSPD: 450kts", font_size=18, color=CYAN)
        self.place_at_grid(hud_text, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(lens),
            Create(grating_lines)
        )
        self.play(
            Create(light_ray),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            TransformFromCopy(light_ray, bent_ray),
            FadeIn(hud_text),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Show 3D visuals concept - rotating cube as a "hologram"
        cube = Cube(side_length=1.0, fill_opacity=0.2, stroke_color=MAGENTA)
        self.place_at_grid(cube, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            card_group.animate.shift(UP*0.5).scale(0.8),
            FadeIn(cube)
        )
        self.play(
            Rotate(cube, angle=2*PI, axis=UP, run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Traditional photos record only the intensity of light waves.",
            "They capture a flat, two-dimensional view of the world.",
            "Holography captures both the intensity and the light's phase.",
            "This records the three-dimensional shape of the light wavefront.",
            "Moving your perspective reveals different angles of the object."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The 3D Mystery: Photo vs. Hologram", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Traditional photos record only the intensity of light waves.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # Camera at B2
        camera_body = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=0.4, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=1)
        camera_lens = Circle(radius=0.1, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=1).shift(UP*0.05)
        camera = VGroup(camera_body, camera_lens)
        self.place_at_grid(camera, "B2")
        
        # Cube (2D representation) at B4
        cube_obj = Square(side_length=0.6, color="#B0C4DE", fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(cube_obj, "B4")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(camera), FadeIn(cube_obj))
        
        # Flash animation
        flash = Flash(self.grid["B4"], color=WHITE, line_length=0.2, num_lines=12)
        self.play(flash)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # They capture a flat, two-dimensional view of the world.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#B0C4DE"))
        
        # 2D result at B6
        photo_rect = Square(side_length=0.6, color="#B0C4DE", fill_opacity=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(photo_rect, "B6")
        label_2d = Text("2D Intensity Map", font_size=18, color="#B0C4DE")
        label_2d.next_to(photo_rect, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        conn_arrow = Arrow(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["B6"], buff=0.4, color="#B0C4DE")
        
        self.play(Create(conn_arrow), FadeIn(photo_rect), Write(label_2d))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Holography captures both the intensity and the light's phase.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        # Laser setup
        laser_box = Rectangle(width=0.5, height=0.3, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(laser_box, "D1")
        
        bs_mirror = Square(side_length=0.4, color=WHITE).rotate(45*DEGREES)
        self.place_at_grid(bs_mirror, "D3")
        
        laser_beam_1 = Line(self.grid["D1"], self.grid["D3"], color="#FF0000", stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(laser_box), FadeIn(bs_mirror))
        self.play(Create(laser_beam_1))
        
        # Split beams
        ref_beam = Line(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["F3"], color="#FF0000", stroke_width=3)
        obj_beam = Line(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["D5"], color="#FF0000", stroke_width=3)
        
        self.play(Create(ref_beam), Create(obj_beam))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # This records the three-dimensional shape of the light wavefront.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#A9A9A9"))
        
        # Plate and wavefronts
        plate_rect = Rectangle(width=0.15, height=1.2, color="#A9A9A9", fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(plate_rect, "F3")
        
        cube_3d_ref = Cube(side_length=0.7, stroke_color="#B0C4DE", fill_opacity=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(cube_3d_ref, "D5")
        
        scattered_beam = Line(self.grid["D5"], self.grid["F3"], color="#FF0000", stroke_width=2)
        
        # Simple wavefront arcs
        wavefronts = VGroup(*[
            Arc(radius=0.2+i*0.2, start_angle=-60*DEGREES, angle=120*DEGREES, color="#A9A9A9")
            for i in range(3)
        ])
        wavefronts.move_to(self.grid["D5"])
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cube_3d_ref), FadeIn(plate_rect))
        self.play(Create(scattered_beam))
        self.play(wavefronts.animate.shift(RIGHT*1.5 + DOWN*1.5).set_opacity(0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Moving your perspective reveals different angles of the object.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # Final 3D hologram emerges in the bottom right area
        hologram = Cube(side_length=1.4, stroke_color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(hologram, "D4", "F6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(hologram))
        
        # Use an updater for continuous rotation to simulate changing perspective
        hologram.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.rotate(dt * 0.8, axis=UP))
        hologram.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.rotate(dt * 0.3, axis=RIGHT))
        
        self.wait(5)
        hologram.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(1)

        self.play(wavefronts.animate.shift(RIGHT*1.5 + DOWN*1.5).set_opacity(0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

# === Section 2 Scene ===
class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lines = [
            "Light waves have both amplitude and phase properties.",
            "Interference happens when two light waves overlap.",
            "Aligned peaks create brightness, while opposing peaks cancel out."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Language of Waves", lines)
        
        # Constants for positioning
        WAVE_TL = "B1"
        WAVE_BR = "E6"
        WAVE_SCALE = 0.35 # Calculated to fit 2 cycles in the right side area
        
        # Trackers for animation
        phase_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        amp_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)

        # Helper to create a sine wave path
        def create_sine_path(phase, amp, color=WHITE):
            # Using 4*PI for two full cycles
            return FunctionGraph(
                lambda x: amp * np.sin(x - phase),
                x_range=[0, 4 * np.pi],
                color=color
            )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A white sine wave #FFFFFF oscillates horizontally across the black background.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Create base wave object
        wave = create_sine_path(0, 1.0, WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(wave, WAVE_TL, WAVE_BR, scale_factor=WAVE_SCALE)
        
        # Updater for smooth oscillation
        def wave_updater(m):
            p = phase_tracker.get_value()
            a = amp_tracker.get_value()
            c = m.get_color()
            # Generate new path data based on current trackers
            new_path = create_sine_path(p, a, c)
            self.place_in_area(new_path, WAVE_TL, WAVE_BR, scale_factor=WAVE_SCALE)
            m.set_points(new_path.get_points())
        
        wave.add_updater(wave_updater)
        self.add(wave)
        
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The peak of the wave flashes yellow #FFFF00 and the trough flashes magenta #FF00FF to show phase.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        )
        
        # Dots that track peak and trough
        peak_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        trough_dot = Dot(color=MAGENTA)
        
        def tracker_dots_updater(group):
            p_dot, t_dot = group
            points = wave.get_points()
            if len(points) > 0:
                # Find the current highest and lowest visible points on the wave path
                peak_idx = np.argmax(points[:, 1])
                trough_idx = np.argmin(points[:, 1])
                p_dot.move_to(points[peak_idx])
                t_dot.move_to(points[trough_idx])
        
        dots_group = VGroup(peak_dot, trough_dot)
        dots_group.add_updater(tracker_dots_updater)
        self.add(dots_group)
        
        # Flash the dots to highlight phase points
        self.play(
            Flash(peak_dot, color="#FFFF00", flash_radius=0.4),
            Flash(trough_dot, color="#FF00FF", flash_radius=0.4),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Continue oscillation to show dots following the wave movement
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(4 * PI), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.remove(dots_group)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Two waves align their peaks, merging into a single wave with double the amplitude in cyan #00FFFF.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        )
        
        # Introduce a second wave to represent overlap/interference
        wave2 = create_sine_path(phase_tracker.get_value(), amp_tracker.get_value(), WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(wave2, WAVE_TL, WAVE_BR, scale_factor=WAVE_SCALE)
        wave2.set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
        
        def wave2_updater(m):
            p = phase_tracker.get_value()
            a = amp_tracker.get_value()
            c = m.get_color()
            new_path = create_sine_path(p, a, c)
            self.place_in_area(new_path, WAVE_TL, WAVE_BR, scale_factor=WAVE_SCALE)
            m.set_points(new_path.get_points())
            
        wave2.add_updater(wave2_updater)
        self.add(wave2)
        
        # Animate constructive interference by merging into a single Cyan wave with double amplitude
        self.play(
            wave.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),
            wave2.animate.set_color("#00FFFF").set_stroke(opacity=1),
            amp_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0),
            phase_tracker.animate.increment_value(PI),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Remove the duplicate wave mobject after they have visually merged
        self.remove(wave2)
        
        # Final result oscillation of the combined wave
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.increment_value(2 * PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(2)

# === Section 2 Scene ===
class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lines = [
            "Light waves have both amplitude and phase properties.",
            "Interference happens when two light waves overlap.",
            "Aligned peaks create brightness, while opposing peaks cancel out."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Language of Waves", lines)
        
        # Constants for positioning
        WAVE_TL = "B1"
        WAVE_BR = "E6"
        WAVE_SCALE = 0.35 # Calculated to fit 2 cycles in the right side area
        
        # Trackers for animation
        phase_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        amp_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)

        # Helper to create a sine wave path
        def create_sine_path(phase, amp, color=WHITE):
            # Using 4*PI for two full cycles
            return FunctionGraph(
                lambda x: amp * np.sin(x - phase),
                x_range=[0, 4 * np.pi],
                color=color
            )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A white sine wave #FFFFFF oscillates horizontally across the black background.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Create base wave object
        wave = create_sine_path(0, 1.0, WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(wave, WAVE_TL, WAVE_BR, scale_factor=WAVE_SCALE)
        
        # Updater for smooth oscillation
        def wave_updater(m):
            p = phase_tracker.get_value()
            a = amp_tracker.get_value()
            c = m.get_color()
            # Generate new path data based on current trackers
            new_path = create_sine_path(p, a, c)
            self.place_in_area(new_path, WAVE_TL, WAVE_BR, scale_factor=WAVE_SCALE)
            m.set_points(new_path.get_points())
        
        wave.add_updater(wave_updater)
        self.add(wave)
        
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The peak of the wave flashes yellow #FFFF00 and the trough flashes magenta #FF00FF to show phase.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        )
        
        # Dots that track peak and trough
        peak_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        trough_dot = Dot(color=MAGENTA)
        
        def tracker_dots_updater(group):
            p_dot, t_dot = group
            points = wave.get_points()
            if len(points) > 0:
                # Find the current highest and lowest visible points on the wave path
                peak_idx = np.argmax(points[:, 1])
                trough_idx = np.argmin(points[:, 1])
                p_dot.move_to(points[peak_idx])
                t_dot.move_to(points[trough_idx])
        
        dots_group = VGroup(peak_dot, trough_dot)
        dots_group.add_updater(tracker_dots_updater)
        self.add(dots_group)
        
        # Flash the dots to highlight phase points
        self.play(
            Flash(peak_dot, color="#FFFF00", flash_radius=0.4),
            Flash(trough_dot, color="#FF00FF", flash_radius=0.4),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Continue oscillation to show dots following the wave movement
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(4 * PI), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.remove(dots_group)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Two waves align their peaks, merging into a single wave with double the amplitude in cyan #00FFFF.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        )

from manim import *
import numpy as np

# === TeachingScene Base Class ===
class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

# === Section 2 Scene ===
class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lines = [
            "Light waves have both amplitude and phase properties.",
            "Interference happens when two light waves overlap.",
            "Aligned peaks create brightness, while opposing peaks cancel out."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Language of Waves", lines)
        
        # Area for waves
        AREA_TL = "B1"
        AREA_BR = "E6"
        
        # Get dimensions for manual point calculation based on grid
        tl_pos = self.grid[AREA_TL]
        br_pos = self.grid[AREA_BR]
        center = (tl_pos + br_pos) / 2
        width = br_pos[0] - tl_pos[0]
        
        # Trackers
        phase_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        amp_tracker = ValueTracker(0.7) # Base amplitude
        
        # Helper to generate points
        def get_sine_points(phase, amplitude):
            num_points = 80
            xs = np.linspace(-width/2, width/2, num_points)
            # freq chosen to show about 2 full cycles in the width
            freq = (2 * 2 * np.pi) / width
            return [center + np.array([x, amplitude * np.sin(freq * x - phase), 0]) for x in xs]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A white sine wave #FFFFFF oscillates horizontally across the black background.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        wave1 = VMobject(color=WHITE)
        wave1.set_points_as_corners(get_sine_points(0, amp_tracker.get_value()))
        
        def wave1_updater(m):
            m.set_points_as_corners(get_sine_points(phase_tracker.get_value(), amp_tracker.get_value()))
            
        wave1.add_updater(wave1_updater)
        self.add(wave1)
        
        # Initial oscillation
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The peak of the wave flashes yellow #FFFF00 and the trough flashes magenta #FF00FF to show phase.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        )
        
        peak_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        trough_dot = Dot(color=MAGENTA)
        
        def dots_updater(group):
            pts = wave1.get_points()
            if len(pts) > 0:
                y_vals = pts[:, 1]
                p_idx = np.argmax(y_vals)
                t_idx = np.argmin(y_vals)
                group[0].move_to(pts[p_idx])
                group[1].move_to(pts[t_idx])
        
        dots = VGroup(peak_dot, trough_dot)
        dots.add_updater(dots_updater)
        self.add(dots)
        
        self.play(
            Flash(peak_dot, color="#FFFF00", flash_radius=0.4),
            Flash(trough_dot, color="#FF00FF", flash_radius=0.4),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Continue oscillation to show dots following the wave
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(4 * PI), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Remove dots before interference part
        self.remove(dots)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Two waves align their peaks, merging into a single wave with double the amplitude in cyan #00FFFF.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        )
        
        # Second wave - starts out of phase (shifted by PI)
        phase_tracker2 = ValueTracker(phase_tracker.get_value() + PI)
        wave2 = VMobject(color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.6)
        
        def wave2_updater(m):
            m.set_points_as_corners(get_sine_points(phase_tracker2.get_value(), amp_tracker.get_value()))
            
        wave2.add_updater(wave2_updater)
        self.add(wave2)
        
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 1. Align phases
        self.play(
            phase_tracker2.animate.set_value(phase_tracker.get_value()),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # 2. Merge: double amplitude and change color to Cyan
        self.play(
            amp_tracker.animate.set_value(1.4),
            wave1.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),
            wave2.animate.set_color("#00FFFF").set_stroke(opacity=0),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        self.remove(wave2)
        
        # Final result oscillation of the combined wave
        final_phase = phase_tracker.get_value() + 2 * PI
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(final_phase), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup layout
        title_text = "Prerequisite: The Language of Waves"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Light waves have both amplitude and phase properties.",
            "Interference happens when two light waves overlap.",
            "Aligned peaks create brightness, while opposing peaks cancel out."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_WAVE = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_PEAK = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_TROUGH = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_INTERFERENCE = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_DIM = "#666666"

        # Position Constants derived from Grid
        grid_b1 = self.grid["B1"]
        grid_b6 = self.grid["B6"]
        grid_e1 = self.grid["E1"]
        
        start_x = float(grid_b1[0])
        end_x = float(grid_b6[0])
        wave_width = end_x - start_x
        center_y = (float(grid_b1[1]) + float(grid_e1[1])) / 2.0
        
        # Dynamic Trackers
        phase_tracker = ValueTracker(0.0)
        amp_tracker = ValueTracker(0.8)
        
        def get_wave_points(p_val, a_val):
            num_steps = 100
            pts = []
            for i in range(num_steps + 1):
                pct = float(i) / num_steps
                x = start_x + pct * wave_width
                # Wave equation: y = center + amp * sin(freq * x - phase)
                # 2 full cycles across the area (4*PI)
                y = center_y + a_val * np.sin(4.0 * np.pi * pct - p_val)
                pts.append([x, y, 0.0])
            return pts

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A white sine wave #FFFFFF oscillates horizontally.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_WAVE)
        
        wave1 = VMobject(color=COLOR_WAVE)
        wave1.set_points_as_corners(get_wave_points(0.0, 0.8))
        wave1.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(
            get_wave_points(phase_tracker.get_value(), amp_tracker.get_value())
        ))
        
        self.add(wave1)
        self.play(
            phase_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0 * np.pi), 
            run_time=3, 
            rate_func=linear
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The peak of the wave flashes yellow #FFFF00 and the trough flashes magenta #FF00FF.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_DIM),
            self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        )
        
        def get_peak_pos():
            p = phase_tracker.get_value()
            # sin(4*pi*pct - p) = 1 => 4*pi*pct - p = pi/2 => pct = (pi/2 + p) / (4*pi)
            pct = (np.pi / 2.0 + p) / (4.0 * np.pi)
            pct = pct % 0.5 # Period in pct is 0.5 (for 2 cycles total)
            return np.array([start_x + pct * wave_width, center_y + amp_tracker.get_value(), 0.0])

        def get_trough_pos():
            p = phase_tracker.get_value()
            # sin(4*pi*pct - p) = -1 => 4*pi*pct - p = 3*pi/2 => pct = (3*pi/2 + p) / (4*pi)
            pct = (3.0 * np.pi / 2.0 + p) / (4.0 * np.pi)
            pct = pct % 0.5
            return np.array([start_x + pct * wave_width, center_y - amp_tracker.get_value(), 0.0])

        peak_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_PEAK, radius=0.08)
        peak_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_peak_pos()))
        
        trough_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_TROUGH, radius=0.08)
        trough_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_trough_pos()))
        
        self.add(peak_dot, trough_dot)
        
        # Flash visual feedback
        self.play(
            Flash(get_peak_pos(), color=COLOR_PEAK, flash_radius=0.3),
            Flash(get_trough_pos(), color=COLOR_TROUGH, flash_radius=0.3),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.play(
            phase_tracker.animate.set_value(4.0 * np.pi), 
            run_time=3, 
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.remove(peak_dot, trough_dot)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Two waves align their peaks, merging into a single wave with double the amplitude in cyan #00FFFF.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_DIM),
            self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_INTERFERENCE)
        )
        
        # Create second wave in anti-phase (destructive interference initially)
        phase_tracker2 = ValueTracker(phase_tracker.get_value() + np.pi)
        wave2 = VMobject(color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.4)
        wave2.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(
            get_wave_points(phase_tracker2.get_value(), 0.8)
        ))
        
        self.add(wave2)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Align the phases (Move to constructive interference)
        self.play(
            phase_tracker2.animate.set_value(phase_tracker.get_value()),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Merge: Fade out second wave and transform first into high-amplitude Cyan wave
        self.play(
            FadeOut(wave2),
            amp_tracker.animate.set_value(1.6),
            wave1.animate.set_color(COLOR_INTERFERENCE),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Final oscillation of the interference result
        self.play(
            phase_tracker.animate.set_value(6.0 * np.pi), 
            run_time=3, 
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: The 3D Mystery: Photo vs. Hologram
section_1.content: Introduction to the fundamental difference between traditional photography and holography. Explain that while photos record only brightness (intensity), holograms record the 'depth' and 'shape' of light waves.
section_1.example: An animated cat tries to pounce on a 2D photo of a mouse and fails to see depth, then encounters a 3D holographic mouse that it can walk around, seeing different angles as it moves.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Waves
section_2.content: Review of wave properties: Amplitude (brightness) and Phase (position in the wave cycle). Introduce Constructive and Destructive Interference as the 'building blocks' of holographic patterns.
section_2.example: Visualizing two pebbles dropped in a pond. Where the ripples meet and get taller is 'constructive' interference; where they cancel out is 'destructive'. Animation shows the peaks and troughs aligning.

section_3.title: The Recording Process: Making the Blueprint
section_3.content: Explain the setup of a laser beam split into two: The 'Object Beam' (hits the subject) and the 'Reference Beam' (stays pure). Their collision creates an 'Interference Pattern' on the film.
section_3.example: A laser beam hits a mirror. Half the light bounces off a 'Golden Dragon' figurine (Object Beam), while the other half hits the film directly (Reference Beam). The film looks like messy noise, not a dragon.

section_4.title: The Physics of Diffraction: Bending the Light
section_4.content: Introducing the concept of Diffraction. When light hits the microscopic 'interference pattern' (which acts like a complex grating), it bends. Introduce the simplified Grating Equation: d sin(θ) = mλ, using graphics to show how spacing (d) affects the angle (θ).
section_4.example: Animation of light passing through a picket fence. If the slats are close together, the light fan-out is wider. The 'messy noise' on the holographic plate is actually a trillion tiny 'fences' that bend light back into the shape of the original object.

section_5.title: Reconstruction: Bringing the Ghost to Life
section_5.content: Explain how shining the Reference Beam back through the processed hologram 'reconstructs' the wavefront of the original object through diffraction.
section_5.example: The 'Golden Dragon' is gone. We shine the laser through the 'noisy' plate. Because of the diffraction math (d sin θ), the light waves exit the plate exactly as they did when they bounced off the dragon. The cat from Section 1 sees the dragon's 'ghost' floating in space.

section_6.title: Real-World Diffraction: From Credit Cards to VR
section_6.content: Brief summary of applications. How microscopic diffraction gratings are used for security and modern head-up displays (HUDs).
section_6.example: Zooming into the shimmering dove on a credit card to show the microscopic lines, then transitioning to a pilot's helmet display showing holographic flight data overlaid on the real world.

section_1.title: The 3D Mystery: Photo vs. Hologram
lecture_lines: Traditional photos record only the intensity of light waves.
They capture a flat, two-dimensional view of the world.
Holography captures both the intensity and the light's phase.
This records the three-dimensional shape of the light wavefront.
Moving your perspective reveals different angles of the object.
animations: A camera #FFFFFF takes a picture of a cube #B0C4DE, creating a flat 2D image.
The flat image is highlighted to show captured light intensity.
A red laser #FF0000 splits, hitting both a cube and plate #A9A9A9.
A complex interference pattern appears on the plate #A9A9A9.
A green 3D cube #00FF00 emerges and rotates from the plate.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Waves
lecture_lines: Light waves have both amplitude and phase properties.
Interference happens when two light waves overlap.
Aligned peaks create brightness, while opposing peaks cancel out.
animations: A white sine wave #FFFFFF oscillates horizontally across the black background.
The peak of the wave flashes yellow #FFFF00 and the trough flashes magenta #FF00FF to show phase.
Two waves align their peaks, merging into a single wave with double the amplitude in cyan #00FFFF.

section_3.title: The Recording Process: Making the Blueprint
lecture_lines: A laser beam is split into two separate paths.
The object beam reflects off the subject being recorded.
The reference beam travels directly to the holographic film.
These beams collide, creating a complex interference pattern.
This microscopic pattern encodes the object's 3D information.
animations: A red laser [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg] #FF0000 splits into two beams at a splitter.
One beam reflects off a teapot [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/teapot.svg] #B0C4DE onto a plate.
A second beam travels directly to the plate as a reference.
Both beams meet, forming an interference pattern #E6E6FA on the plate.
Zoom into the plate showing microscopic details of the pattern.

section_4.title: The Physics of Diffraction: Bending the Light
lecture_lines: Diffraction bends light as it passes through tiny openings.
Holographic patterns act as microscopic gratings for light waves.
This bending recreates the original path of the light.
animations: Parallel white wave fronts #FFFFFF approach a narrow vertical [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slit.svg] slit.
As the waves pass through, they transform into orange circular arcs #FFA500 spreading outward.

Multiple [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slit.svg] slits appear, creating a pattern of bright and dark spots #FF6347 on a distant [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/screen.svg] screen.

section_5.title: Reconstruction: Bringing the Ghost to Life
lecture_lines: To see the image, we use the reference beam.
Illuminating the hologram causes the light to diffract.
The diffracted light waves perfectly mimic the original object.
We see a three-dimensional "ghost" of the recorded object.
The original wavefront is recreated, restoring depth and perspective.
animations: A red laser #FF0000 [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg] shines through a holographic plate.
Blue light rays #87CEEB diffract and bend through the plate.
The light rays reconstruct the original object's complex wavefront.
A shimmering virtual teapot #F0FFF0 [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/teapot.svg] appears in mid-air.
The teapot #F0FFF0 [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/teapot.svg] rotates, revealing its three-dimensional structure.

section_6.title: Real-World Diffraction: From Credit Cards to VR
lecture_lines: Tiny diffraction gratings provide security on credit cards.
Head-up displays use these principles to project transparent data.
Holography brings 3D visuals to modern engineering and art.
animations: A silver credit card #C0C0C0 is shown with a bird-shaped hologram in the corner.
The card tilts, and the bird's color shifts smoothly from red #FF0000 to blue #0000FF.
A cross-section of a VR lens appears, showing light bending through tiny gratings #98FB98.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Traditional photos record only the intensity of light waves.",
            "They capture a flat, two-dimensional view of the world.",
            "Holography captures both the intensity and the light's phase.",
            "This records the three-dimensional shape of the light wavefront.",
            "Moving your perspective reveals different angles of the object."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The 3D Mystery: Photo vs. Hologram", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Traditional photos record only the intensity of light waves.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # Camera at B2
        camera_body = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=0.4, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=1)
        camera_lens = Circle(radius=0.1, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=1).shift(UP*0.05)
        camera = VGroup(camera_body, camera_lens)
        self.place_at_grid(camera, "B2")
        
        # Cube (2D representation) at B4
        cube_obj = Square(side_length=0.6, color="#B0C4DE", fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(cube_obj, "B4")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(camera), FadeIn(cube_obj))
        
        # Flash animation
        flash = Flash(self.grid["B4"], color=WHITE, line_length=0.2, num_lines=12)
        self.play(flash)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # They capture a flat, two-dimensional view of the world.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#B0C4DE"))
        
        # 2D result at B6
        photo_rect = Square(side_length=0.6, color="#B0C4DE", fill_opacity=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(photo_rect, "B6")
        label_2d = Text("2D Intensity Map", font_size=18, color="#B0C4DE")
        label_2d.next_to(photo_rect, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        conn_arrow = Arrow(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["B6"], buff=0.4, color="#B0C4DE")
        
        self.play(Create(conn_arrow), FadeIn(photo_rect), Write(label_2d))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Holography captures both the intensity and the light's phase.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        # Laser setup
        laser_box = Rectangle(width=0.5, height=0.3, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(laser_box, "D1")
        
        bs_mirror = Square(side_length=0.4, color=WHITE).rotate(45*DEGREES)
        self.place_at_grid(bs_mirror, "D3")
        
        laser_beam_1 = Line(self.grid["D1"], self.grid["D3"], color="#FF0000", stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(laser_box), FadeIn(bs_mirror))
        self.play(Create(laser_beam_1))
        
        # Split beams
        ref_beam = Line(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["F3"], color="#FF0000", stroke_width=3)
        obj_beam = Line(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["D5"], color="#FF0000", stroke_width=3)
        
        self.play(Create(ref_beam), Create(obj_beam))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # This records the three-dimensional shape of the light wavefront.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#A9A9A9"))
        
        # Plate and wavefronts
        plate_rect = Rectangle(width=0.15, height=1.2, color="#A9A9A9", fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(plate_rect, "F3")
        
        cube_3d_ref = Cube(side_length=0.7, stroke_color="#B0C4DE", fill_opacity=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(cube_3d_ref, "D5")
        
        scattered_beam = Line(self.grid["D5"], self.grid["F3"], color="#FF0000", stroke_width=2)
        
        # Simple wavefront arcs
        wavefronts = VGroup(*[
            Arc(radius=0.2+i*0.2, start_angle=-60*DEGREES, angle=120*DEGREES, color="#A9A9A9")
            for i in range(3)
        ])
        wavefronts.move_to(self.grid["D5"])
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cube_3d_ref), FadeIn(plate_rect))
        self.play(Create(scattered_beam))
        self.play(wavefronts.animate.shift(RIGHT*1.5 + DOWN*1.5).set_opacity(0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Moving your perspective reveals different angles of the object.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # Final 3D hologram emerges in the bottom right area
        hologram = Cube(side_length=1.4, stroke_color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(hologram, "D4", "F6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(hologram))
        
        # Use an updater for continuous rotation to simulate changing perspective
        hologram.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.rotate(dt * 0.8, axis=UP))
        hologram.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.rotate(dt * 0.3, axis=RIGHT))
        
        self.wait(5)
        hologram.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # --- Data Setup ---
        title_text = "Prerequisite: The Language of Waves"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Light waves have both amplitude and phase properties.",
            "Interference happens when two light waves overlap.",
            "Aligned peaks create brightness, while opposing peaks cancel out."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_WAVE = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_PEAK = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_TROUGH = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_INTERFERENCE = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_DIM = "#666666"

        # Wave boundary points using grid positions C1 to C6
        start_pt = self.grid["C1"]
        end_pt = self.grid["C6"]
        start_x = float(start_pt[0])
        end_x = float(end_pt[0])
        wave_y = float(start_pt[1])
        wave_width = end_x - start_x

        # Trackers for animation
        phase_tracker = ValueTracker(0.0)
        amp_tracker = ValueTracker(0.7)
        phase_tracker2 = ValueTracker(np.pi) # Second wave offset for initial interference

        def get_wave_points(phase, amp):
            res = 80
            pts = []
            for i in range(res + 1):
                pct = float(i) / res
                curr_x = start_x + pct * wave_width
                # Wave equation: y = baseline + amp * sin(2*pi*cycles*pct - phase)
                # 2 cycles across the width
                curr_y = wave_y + float(amp) * np.sin(4.0 * np.pi * pct - float(phase))
                pts.append([curr_x, curr_y, 0.0])
            return pts

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A white sine wave #FFFFFF oscillates horizontally.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_WAVE), run_time=0.5)
        
        wave1 = VMobject(color=COLOR_WAVE)
        wave1.set_points_as_corners(get_wave_points(0.0, 0.7))
        wave1.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(
            get_wave_points(phase_tracker.get_value(), amp_tracker.get_value())
        ))
        
        self.add(wave1)
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0 * np.pi), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The peak of the wave flashes yellow #FFFF00 and the trough flashes magenta #FF00FF.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_DIM),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        peak_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_PEAK, radius=0.1)
        trough_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_TROUGH, radius=0.1)

        def update_peak(d):
            p = float(phase_tracker.get_value())
            amp = float(amp_tracker.get_value())
            # sin(4*pi*pct - p) = 1 => 4*pi*pct - p = pi/2 => pct = (pi/2 + p) / (4*pi)
            pct = (np.pi / 2.0 + p) / (4.0 * np.pi)
            pct = pct % 0.5 # Period is 0.5 in pct units
            d.move_to([start_x + pct * wave_width, wave_y + amp, 0.0])

        def update_trough(d):
            p = float(phase_tracker.get_value())
            amp = float(amp_tracker.get_value())
            # sin(4*pi*pct - p) = -1 => 4*pi*pct - p = 3*pi/2 => pct = (3*pi/2 + p) / (4*pi)
            pct = (1.5 * np.pi + p) / (4.0 * np.pi)
            pct = pct % 0.5
            d.move_to([start_x + pct * wave_width, wave_y - amp, 0.0])

        peak_dot.add_updater(update_peak)
        trough_dot.add_updater(update_trough)
        
        self.add(peak_dot, trough_dot)
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(4.0 * np.pi), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.remove(peak_dot, trough_dot)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Two waves align their peaks, merging into a single wave with double the amplitude in cyan #00FFFF.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_DIM),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_INTERFERENCE),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        # Introduce secondary wave (initially out of phase)
        wave2 = VMobject(color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.4)
        wave2.set_points_as_corners(get_wave_points(phase_tracker2.get_value(), 0.7))
        wave2.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(
            get_wave_points(phase_tracker2.get_value(), 0.7)
        ))
        
        self.add(wave2)
        self.wait(1.0)

        # Phase alignment (Transition to constructive interference)
        self.play(
            phase_tracker2.animate.set_value(phase_tracker.get_value()),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Merge: increase amplitude of first wave and fade out the second
        # Note: both are driven by updaters, so we just animate the tracker
        self.play(
            FadeOut(wave2),
            amp_tracker.animate.set_value(1.4),
            wave1.animate.set_color(COLOR_INTERFERENCE),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        
        # Final oscillation of the constructive interference result
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(6.0 * np.pi), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2.0)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Recording Process: Making the Blueprint", [
            "A laser beam is split into two separate paths.",
            "The object beam reflects off the subject being recorded.",
            "The reference beam travels directly to the holographic film.",
            "These beams collide, creating a complex interference pattern.",
            "This microscopic pattern encodes the object's 3D information."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        laser_color = "#FF0000"
        teapot_color = "#B0C4DE"
        fringe_color = "#E6E6FA"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A red laser #FF0000 splits into two beams at a splitter.
        source = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(source, "B1")
        source_label = Text("Laser", font_size=16).next_to(source, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        splitter = Rectangle(height=0.6, width=0.1, color=WHITE).rotate(45*DEGREES)
        self.place_at_grid(splitter, "B2")
        splitter_label = Text("Splitter", font_size=14).next_to(splitter, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        initial_beam = Line(self.grid["B1"], self.grid["B2"], color=laser_color)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(source), FadeIn(source_label), FadeIn(splitter), FadeIn(splitter_label))
        self.play(Create(initial_beam))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # One beam reflects off a teapot #B0C4DE onto a plate.
        teapot_body = Ellipse(width=0.6, height=0.4, color=teapot_color, fill_opacity=0.6)
        teapot_handle = Arc(radius=0.15, start_angle=-PI/2, angle=PI, color=teapot_color).shift(RIGHT*0.3)
        teapot_spout = Line(LEFT*0.3, LEFT*0.5 + UP*0.2, color=teapot_color)
        teapot = VGroup(teapot_body, teapot_handle, teapot_spout)
        self.place_at_grid(teapot, "B5")
        teapot_label = Text("Teapot", font_size=16, color=teapot_color).next_to(teapot, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        plate = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=0.2, color=GREY_A, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(plate, "E6")
        plate_label = Text("Film", font_size=16).next_to(plate, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        object_beam_part1 = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B5"], color=laser_color)
        object_beam_part2 = Line(self.grid["B5"], self.grid["E6"], color=laser_color)
        obj_label = Text("Object Beam", font_size=12, color=laser_color).next_to(object_beam_part1, UP, buff=0.05)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(teapot), FadeIn(teapot_label), FadeIn(plate), FadeIn(plate_label))
        self.play(Create(object_beam_part1), FadeIn(obj_label))
        self.play(Create(object_beam_part2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # A second beam travels directly to the plate as a reference.
        mirror = Rectangle(height=0.4, width=0.05, color=WHITE).rotate(45*DEGREES)
        self.place_at_grid(mirror, "E2")
        mirror_label = Text("Mirror", font_size=14).next_to(mirror, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        ref_beam_part1 = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["E2"], color=laser_color)
        ref_beam_part2 = Line(self.grid["E2"], self.grid["E6"], color=laser_color)
        ref_label = Text("Reference Beam", font_size=12, color=laser_color).next_to(ref_beam_part2, DOWN, buff=0.05)
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(mirror), FadeIn(mirror_label))
        self.play(Create(ref_beam_part1))
        self.play(Create(ref_beam_part2), FadeIn(ref_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Both beams meet, forming an interference pattern #E6E6FA on the plate.
        fringes = VGroup(*[
            Line(UP*0.7, DOWN*0.7, color=fringe_color, stroke_width=0.8).shift(RIGHT * x)
            for x in np.linspace(-0.06, 0.06, 12)
        ])
        fringes.move_to(plate.get_center())
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(fringes))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Zoom into the plate showing microscopic details of the pattern.
        zoom_pattern = VGroup()
        for i in range(25):
            x_off = -2.5 + i * 0.2
            pts = [np.array([x_off + 0.1 * np.sin(y * 3 + i), y, 0]) for y in np.linspace(-2.5, 2.5, 30)]
            line = VMobject(color=fringe_color, stroke_width=1.5)
            line.set_points_as_corners(pts)
            zoom_pattern.add(line)
        
        self.place_in_area(zoom_pattern, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        setup_group = VGroup(source, source_label, splitter, splitter_label, initial_beam, 
                            teapot, teapot_label, plate, plate_label, object_beam_part1, object_beam_part2,
                            obj_label, mirror, mirror_label, ref_beam_part1, ref_beam_part2, ref_label, fringes)
        
        self.play(
            setup_group.animate.set_opacity(0),
            FadeIn(zoom_pattern)
        )
        self.wait(3)
        
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

            FadeIn(grating),
            Write(equation),
            arcs.animate.scale(1.3).shift(RIGHT * 0.3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREY),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF6347")
        )
        
        # Ddistant screen at column 6

        self.place_at_grid(screen, "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Interference pattern: Bright spots (Central maximum is brightest)
        spots = VGroup()
        for i in range(-3, 4):
            # Diminishing intensity for higher order spots
            opacity = 1.0 if i == 0 else (0.7 if abs(i) == 1 else (0.4 if abs(i) == 2 else 0.2))
            dot = Dot(color="#FF6347", radius=0.18).set_opacity(opacity)
            spots.add(dot.shift(UP * i * 0.75))
        self.place_at_grid(spots, "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Light rays from grating to spots to visualize the "bending"
        grating_pos = self.grid["C3"]
        rays = VGroup(*[
            Line(grating_pos, spot.get_center(), color="#FF6347", stroke_width=1).set_opacity(0.3)
            for spot in spots
        ])
        
        self.play(
            Create(screen),
            LaggedStart(*[Create(r) for r in rays], lag_ratio=0.1),
            FadeIn(spots, shift=RIGHT*0.2),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # --- Data Setup ---
        title_text = "Prerequisite: The Language of Waves"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Light waves have both amplitude and phase properties.",
            "Interference happens when two light waves overlap.",
            "Aligned peaks create brightness, while opposing peaks cancel out."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_WAVE = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_PEAK = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_TROUGH = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_INTERFERENCE = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_DIM = "#666666"

        # Wave boundary points using grid positions C1 to C6
        start_pt = self.grid["C1"]
        end_pt = self.grid["C6"]
        start_x = float(start_pt[0])
        end_x = float(end_pt[0])
        wave_y = float(start_pt[1])
        wave_width = end_x - start_x

        # Trackers for animation
        phase_tracker = ValueTracker(0.0)
        amp_tracker = ValueTracker(0.7)
        phase_tracker2 = ValueTracker(np.pi) # Second wave offset for initial interference

        def get_wave_points(phase, amp):
            res = 80
            pts = []
            for i in range(res + 1):
                pct = float(i) / res
                curr_x = start_x + pct * wave_width
                # Wave equation: y = baseline + amp * sin(2*pi*cycles*pct - phase)
                # 2 cycles across the width
                curr_y = wave_y + float(amp) * np.sin(4.0 * np.pi * pct - float(phase))
                pts.append([curr_x, curr_y, 0.0])
            return pts

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A white sine wave #FFFFFF oscillates horizontally.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_WAVE), run_time=0.5)
        
        wave1 = VMobject(color=COLOR_WAVE)
        wave1.set_points_as_corners(get_wave_points(0.0, 0.7))
        wave1.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(
            get_wave_points(phase_tracker.get_value(), amp_tracker.get_value())
        ))
        
        self.add(wave1)
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0 * np.pi), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The peak of the wave flashes yellow #FFFF00 and the trough flashes magenta #FF00FF.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_DIM),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        peak_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_PEAK, radius=0.1)
        trough_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_TROUGH, radius=0.1)

        def update_peak(d):
            p = float(phase_tracker.get_value())
            amp = float(amp_tracker.get_value())
            # sin(4*pi*pct - p) = 1 => 4*pi*pct - p = pi/2 => pct = (pi/2 + p) / (4*pi)
            pct = (np.pi / 2.0 + p) / (4.0 * np.pi)
            pct = pct % 0.5 # Period is 0.5 in pct units
            d.move_to([start_x + pct * wave_width, wave_y + amp, 0.0])

        def update_trough(d):
            p = float(phase_tracker.get_value())
            amp = float(amp_tracker.get_value())
            # sin(4*pi*pct - p) = -1 => 4*pi*pct - p = 3*pi/2 => pct = (3*pi/2 + p) / (4*pi)
            pct = (1.5 * np.pi + p) / (4.0 * np.pi)
            pct = pct % 0.5
            d.move_to([start_x + pct * wave_width, wave_y - amp, 0.0])

        peak_dot.add_updater(update_peak)
        trough_dot.add_updater(update_trough)
        
        self.add(peak_dot, trough_dot)
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(4.0 * np.pi), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.remove(peak_dot, trough_dot)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Two waves align their peaks, merging into a single wave with double the amplitude in cyan #00FFFF.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_DIM),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_INTERFERENCE),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        # Introduce secondary wave (initially out of phase)
        wave2 = VMobject(color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.4)
        wave2.set_points_as_corners(get_wave_points(phase_tracker2.get_value(), 0.7))
        wave2.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(
            get_wave_points(phase_tracker2.get_value(), 0.7)
        ))
        
        self.add(wave2)
        self.wait(1.0)

        # Phase alignment (Transition to constructive interference)
        self.play(
            phase_tracker2.animate.set_value(phase_tracker.get_value()),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Merge: increase amplitude of first wave and fade out the second
        # Note: both are driven by updaters, so we just animate the tracker
        self.play(
            FadeOut(wave2),
            amp_tracker.animate.set_value(1.4),
            wave1.animate.set_color(COLOR_INTERFERENCE),
            run_time=2.0
        )
        
        # Final oscillation of the constructive interference result
        self.play(phase_tracker.animate.set_value(6.0 * np.pi), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2.0)

outline.title: The 3D Mystery: Photo vs. Hologram
outline.content: Introduction to the fundamental difference between traditional photography and holography. Explain that while photos record only brightness (intensity), holograms record the 'depth' and 'shape' of light waves.
outline.example: An animated cat tries to pounce on a 2D photo of a mouse and fails to see depth, then encounters a 3D holographic mouse that it can walk around, seeing different angles as it moves.

storyboard.title: The 3D Mystery: Photo vs. Hologram
lecture_lines: Traditional photos record only the intensity of light waves.
They capture a flat, two-dimensional view of the world.
Holography captures both the intensity and the light's phase.
This records the three-dimensional shape of the light wavefront.
Moving your perspective reveals different angles of the object.
animations: A camera #FFFFFF takes a picture of a cube #B0C4DE, creating a flat 2D image.
The flat image is highlighted to show captured light intensity.
A red laser #FF0000 splits, hitting both a cube and plate #A9A9A9.
A complex interference pattern appears on the plate #A9A9A9.
A green 3D cube #00FF00 emerges and rotates from the plate.

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "The Physics of Diffraction: Bending the Light"
        lines = [
            "Diffraction bends light as it passes through tiny openings.",
            "Holographic patterns act as microscopic gratings for light waves.",
            "This bending recreates the original path of the light."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Parallel white wave fronts #FFFFFF approach a narrow vertical slit.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Slit setup: A barrier with a small gap
        slit_top = Line(UP*1.5, UP*0.15, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        slit_bottom = Line(DOWN*0.15, DOWN*1.5, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        slit_barrier = VGroup(slit_top, slit_bottom)
        self.place_at_grid(slit_barrier, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Incoming wave fronts
        wave_fronts = VGroup(*[
            Line(UP*1.2, DOWN*1.2, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=2)
            for _ in range(4)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(wave_fronts, "C1", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Animate waves approaching the slit
        self.add(slit_barrier, wave_fronts)
        self.play(
            wave_fronts.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.8),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # As the waves pass through, they transform into orange circular arcs #FFA500 spreading outward.
        # Holographic patterns act as microscopic gratings for light waves.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GREY),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFA500")
        )
        
        # Create orange circular arcs centered at the slit
        slit_center = self.grid["C3"]
        arcs = VGroup(*[
            Arc(
                radius=r, 
                start_angle=-PI/3, 
                angle=2*PI/3, 
                arc_center=slit_center, 
                color="#FFA500",
                stroke_width=3
            ) for r in [0.2, 0.6, 1.0, 1.4]
        ])
        
        # Transition from straight waves to arcs
        self.play(
            FadeOut(wave_fronts),
            Create(arcs),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Introduce multiple slits (grating) and the grating equation
        grating = VGroup()
        for i in range(-6, 7):
            grating.add(Line(LEFT*0.15, RIGHT*0.15, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).shift(UP*i*0.25))
        grating.rotate(PI/2)
        self.place_at_grid(grating, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        equation = MathTex("d \\sin(\\theta) = m\\lambda", color="#FFA500", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "A5")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(slit_barrier),
            FadeIn(grating),
            Write(equation),
            arcs.animate.scale(1.3).shift(RIGHT * 0.3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Multiple slits appear, creating a pattern of bright and dark spots #FF6347 on a distant screen.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREY),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF6347")
        )
        
        # Ddistant screen at column 6

        self.place_at_grid(screen, "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Interference pattern: Bright spots (Central maximum is brightest)
        spots = VGroup()
        for i in range(-3, 4):
            # Diminishing intensity for higher order spots
            opacity = 1.0 if i == 0 else (0.7 if abs(i) == 1 else (0.4 if abs(i) == 2 else 0.2))
            dot = Dot(color="#FF6347", radius=0.18).set_opacity(opacity)
            spots.add(dot.shift(UP * i * 0.75))
        self.place_at_grid(spots, "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Light rays from grating to spots to visualize the "bending"
        grating_pos = self.grid["C3"]
        rays = VGroup(*[
            Line(grating_pos, spot.get_center(), color="#FF6347", stroke_width=1).set_opacity(0.3)
            for spot in spots
        ])
        
        self.play(
            Create(screen),
            LaggedStart(*[Create(r) for r in rays], lag_ratio=0.1),
            FadeIn(spots, shift=RIGHT*0.2),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: The Recording Process: Making the Blueprint
outline.content: Explain the setup of a laser beam split into two: The 'Object Beam' (hits the subject) and the 'Reference Beam' (stays pure). Their collision creates an 'Interference Pattern' on the film.
outline.example: A laser beam hits a mirror. Half the light bounces off a 'Golden Dragon' figurine (Object Beam), while the other half hits the film directly (Reference Beam). The film looks like messy noise, not a dragon.

storyboard.title: The Recording Process: Making the Blueprint
lecture_lines: A laser beam is split into two separate paths.
The object beam reflects off the subject being recorded.
The reference beam travels directly to the holographic film.
These beams collide, creating a complex interference pattern.
This microscopic pattern encodes the object's 3D information.
animations: A red laser [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg] #FF0000 splits into two beams at a splitter.
One beam reflects off a teapot [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/teapot.svg] #B0C4DE onto a plate.
A second beam travels directly to the plate as a reference.
Both beams meet, forming an interference pattern #E6E6FA on the plate.
